programs.name: El Salvador
programs.bitcoin_integration: El Salvador was the first country to make Bitcoin legal tender (Sept 7, 2021). Under a $1.4bn / 40-month IMF program (Dec 2024), Legislative Decree No. 199 was gazetted Jan 30 2025 and took effect ~May 1 2025, dismantling the compulsory framework: merchant acceptance of Bitcoin is now voluntary (not mandatory), the government's Chivo wallet participation is being phased out (by end-July 2025 per IMF terms), and the state does not voluntarily accumulate more Bitcoin. As of 2026 Bitcoin is effectively voluntary tender — most analysts treat the compulsory 'legal tender' obligation as rescinded while the USD remains the dominant currency for wages, prices and taxes; the state retains its existing Bitcoin holdings. The country remains strongly crypto-promotional at the government level despite the legal rollback.

finance.tax_benefits:
Favorable crypto tax treatment; legal-tender status revoked in Feb 2025 (IMF condition) — sovereign-signal framing is now historical, but no capital gains tax on Bitcoin in many cases remains.

Crypto/Bitcoin tax: No capital gains tax on Bitcoin exchanges — the 2025 Decree No. 199 reform explicitly retains/exempts Bitcoin exchanges from capital gains tax (Bloomberg Tax). Since the reform, taxes and government monetary obligations must be paid in US dollars (Bitcoin is no longer accepted for taxes, and the state's automatic USD conversion obligation was removed); the country is dollarized. El Salvador uses a territorial tax system focused on domestic-source income.
finance.bitcoin_specific: Yes — but only for the government's Freedom Visa citizenship-by-investment contribution: the ~USD 1 million development-fund contribution can be paid in Bitcoin or USDT. Since the 2025 reform, taxes and general government fees/obligations are payable in US dollars only, not Bitcoin. General visa/immigration fees are in USD.

programs.name: Portugal
programs.bitcoin_integration: Bitcoin is legal and unregulated as a currency in Portugal. Portugal was historically one of the most crypto-friendly jurisdictions in the EU (tax-free crypto until 2023). Since 1 January 2023 (State Budget Law 24-D/2022) a crypto-asset tax regime applies: capital gains on crypto held for less than 365 days are taxed as Category G gains at a flat 28% (or included in aggregated income), while gains on crypto held for 365 days or more are excluded from tax for most residents. The Portuguese Tax Authority (Autoridade Tributária) issued official guidance and binding rulings (e.g. Processo 29052) confirming this.

finance.tax_benefits:
Changes in 2023-2025 reduced some benefits. Still territorial elements and quality of life high.

Crypto/Bitcoin tax: Since 2023, short-term crypto capital gains (<365 days holding) taxed at flat 28% (Category G); residents may elect aggregation into progressive income brackets. Long-term gains (>=365 days) tax-exempt in most cases (exclusion under Art. 10(19) CIRS applies to transactions with EU/EEA or info-exchange countries). Category E capital income from crypto taxed at special 28% rate; mining/validation treated as business income (Category B). Crypto holdings must be declared annually (Portaria 39-B/2024). No capital gains tax on long-held bitcoin is the key favourable feature.
finance.bitcoin_specific: No official acceptance of BTC for golden-visa or government/immigration fees; all AIMA application and visa fees are payable in EUR (standard and 25%-reduced digital rates). Qualifying golden-visa investments (funds, research, company capital, cultural donation) must be in EUR. A privately proposed crypto-backed fund route (e.g. Unbound Fund marketing 'bitcoin-backed golden visa') has not been approved or confirmed by Portuguese authorities.

programs.details: Lifestyle + residency strong, but tax/crypto policy has shifted. Requires fresh research for MotoPass. Modeled minimum investment $250,000 (typical $400,000). Primary routes on file: Golden Visa (investment fund route), D7 passive income. Tax notes: Changes in 2023-2025 reduced some benefits. Still territorial elements and quality of life high. Verify every figure against primary sources and Satohash proofs before acting.
sources: Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (AT) - Portugal Tax Authority — https://info.portaldasfinancas.gov.pt/pt/apoio_contribuinte/Folhetos_informativos/Documents/Criptoativos.pdf

pathways.label: Golden Visa (investment fund route)

programs.name: Italy
programs.bitcoin_integration: Bitcoin and crypto ('cripto-attività') are legal in Italy and recognized as an autonomous asset class under Article 67(1)(c-sexies) of the TUIR since 1 January 2023 (2023 Budget Law 197/2022). Italy's stance is neutral-to-sceptical: gains are taxed and the Agenzia delle Entrate has automated oversight; there is no special crypto-industry incentive and no official bitcoin-friendly policy.

finance.tax_benefits:
Standard OECD-aligned framework; specialist planning recommended.

Crypto/Bitcoin tax: Italian tax residents pay a flat substitute tax on realized crypto capital gains - 26% for gains realized 2023-2025, rising to 33% for gains realized from 1 January 2026 (Law 207/2024 / 2025 Budget Law; per several 2026 guides), with no EUR 2,000 exemption from 2026 (taxable from first euro). A 26% carve-out applies to MiCAR-compliant euro-denominated e-money-token stablecoins. Foreign-held crypto is subject to a 0.2% wealth tax and Quadro RW declaration (no de minimis). Staking/mining income is treated as personal income (IRPEF). DAC8 (D.Lgs. 194/2025) obliges crypto service providers to report Italian users from 1 January 2026. CAVEAT: sources disagree on the effective timing of the 33% rate - some date it from 1 Jan 2026, others cite a rise planned for 2027; verify against Agenzia delle Entrate.
finance.bitcoin_specific: No official acceptance of BTC for Italian visa, residence-permit, or Investor Visa ('golden visa') fees; visa, stamp and permit charges are paid in EUR. Qualifying investments (startup, company, bonds, donation) must be made in EUR through Italian financial channels. Bitcoin cannot be used to satisfy any investor-visa route.

programs.bitcoin_integration: Bitcoin (and crypto) is legal in Ireland and fully recognized in tax law, but Receipt of Revenue guidance is neutral and non-promotional: there are no special tax rules for crypto-assets, and they are treated under general income tax, Capital Gains Tax and CAT principles. Revenue endorsed the CJEU Hedqvist ruling that bitcoin is exempt from VAT as a currency-like negotiable instrument. Ireland is aligned with EU DAC8/CARF automatic reporting of crypto from 1 January 2026; there is no bitcoin-friendly tax incentive.

finance.tax_benefits:
Standard OECD-aligned framework; specialist planning recommended.

Crypto/Bitcoin tax: Revenue applies no crypto-specific regime: (1) profits from selling crypto are generally capital gains taxable at the standard CGT rate (33%) for Irish-resident individuals; gains may be subject to income tax (through IRPF-style treatment) if trading amounts to a business/trade. (2) Crypto income (e.g. mining or payment for services, where in the course of a trade/profession) is taxable income. (3) Gifts/inheritance of crypto fall under Capital Acquisitions Tax (33% threshold-based). (4) Bitcoin is VAT-exempt (Hedqvist C-264/14); VAT applies to goods/services sold for bitcoin at the euro value. (5) From 1 January 2026 reporting crypto-asset service providers must report Irish clients under CARF/DAC8. No exemption for long-term holdings exists (unlike Portugal).
finance.bitcoin_specific: No official acceptance of BTC for Irish visa, residence-permit, or any government/immigration fees; all charges are in EUR. The Immigrant Investor Programme (the former investment-linked residency route) is closed, and its fees/investments were in EUR only. Bitcoin cannot be used to obtain any Irish residency permission.

programs.bitcoin_integration: Panama has NO enacted comprehensive crypto law and Bitcoin is NOT legal tender. Its constitution 'Monetary Freedom' (Article 262) forbids compulsory legal tender, meaning any currency — including crypto — can circulate by private agreement but the state does not give Bitcoin legal-tender status. Bill No. 697 (2021) passed the National Assembly in April 2022 but was vetoed by President Cortizo in June 2022 over AML/oversight and constitutional concerns. A successor, Bill No. 247 (introduced 2025), would create a FATF-aligned registration/licensing regime for Virtual Asset Service Providers (VASPs), recognize crypto as a valid medium of exchange by agreement, and set up a public registry and suspicious-operation reporting; it remained pending (not enacted) as of 2026. Panama positions itself as a permissive, business-friendly crypto jurisdiction (regional hub for tokenization/real-estate) but without dedicated legislation in force.

finance.tax_benefits:
Territorial taxation — foreign income often not taxed. Very attractive for Bitcoin holders.

There is no specific crypto-tax statute; crypto gains derived from offshore activity are generally not subject to Panamanian income tax. Bitcoin/crypto is commonly regarded as not taxed on foreign-source capital gains.

programs.bitcoin_integration: Mexico regulates crypto under the 2018 Law to Regulate Financial Technology Institutions ('Fintech Law' / LRITF) which defines 'virtual assets', elaborated by Banxico Circular 4/2019. Non-financial individuals and companies may legally own, hold, trade and exchange crypto and operate exchanges/custodians without a specific license (subject to AML obligations; a July 16 2025 AML-law reform classifies VASPs as Designated Non-Financial Businesses with travel-rule, KYC and transaction-reporting duties). programs.bitcoin_integration: Minimal/no formal crypto policy. The new CBI programme (Decreto-Lei n.º 07/2025 under Nationality Law n.º 07/2022) requires the USD 90,000+ contribution to be made into the National Transformation Fund's bank account, nominally in US dollars (the national currency is the dobra, STN). In September 2025 the CIU announced a partnership to make the program 'the world's first blockchain-enabled citizenship-by-investment program' (a technical/process innovation), and crypto assets are accepted as PROOF OF SOURCE OF FUNDS - but there is no official government stance on Bitcoin as policy, and neither Bitcoin nor crypto is legal tender.

finance.tax_benefits:
Low-key tax regime on a small island economy; seek specialist planning. No substance requirement beyond the contribution under the CBI program as marketed by licensed agents.

Crypto/Bitcoin tax: Territorial/limited-tax regime favourable to non-residents: non-residents are taxed only on income sourced within the country and pay no tax on foreign-source income, capital gains, inheritance or wealth; residents face 0-32% on worldwide income; corporate tax ~25% (10% for priority development sectors); VAT 15%. There is no dedicated Bitcoin/crypto tax rule documented - crypto gains of non-residents are not domestically taxed, but this reflects the broad territorial regime and an absence of crypto-specific law rather than an explicit crypto policy.
finance.bitcoin_specific: Indirect only - official contributions and CIU fees are payable to the National Transformation Fund's bank account in US dollars; licensed agents may accept cryptocurrency as proof of source of funds (and in practice some agents settle in crypto on the client's behalf before paying authorities in USD), but there is no official direct-Bitcoin payment route.

programs.details:
São Tomé and Príncipe operates a Citizenship by Investment programme via a contribution to the national development fund: minimum ~USD 90,000–95,000 single applicant, fully remote with NO residence, physical-presence, travel or language requirement. Processing advertised at around six weeks. Applicants must be 18+, in good health, with clean criminal record and a provable source of funds; a USD ~5,000 submission fee applies (USD ~5,000 per additional dependent). Program is newer and smaller than the Caribbean CBI bloc; rules should be verified against official/embassy channels before structuring. Single route = non-refundable National Transformation Fund contribution USD 90,000 single / 95,000 family of 2-4 / +5,000 per extra dependent; +5,000 due-diligence fee. Fully remote (no residency/visit/language/interview); dual citizenship; CPLP mobility (Portugal, Brazil). Restrictions (Apr 2026): applicants with 3+ foreign nationalities barred; naturalised citizens acquiring a 4th lose nationality; adult-dependent passport issuance frozen. Licensed agents only. Advertised 6-8 wks; real-world 4-6+ months.
